query: Target-conditioned retrieval from category/brand/action/time histories when exact target-category matches are absent: DIN and DMR primary methods; field-context query construction, QueryFormer capacity-matched query replacements, and UniDot direct relevance readout controls.
question: Why does target-aware history attention add little over pooling when the target category is absent from history, and can available field context recover useful cross-category or brand/action evidence? In the supplied single-seed validation receipts, AUC rises from 0.6050036145 (static) to 0.6102261137 (pooled) to 0.6133619861 (DIN). DIN minus pooled is 0.0026743907 for category-match-present histories (2,516,922 samples; 129,821 positives; 2,387,101 negatives), versus 0.0002617450 for category-match-absent histories (717,129 samples; 29,616 positives; 687,513 negatives). This is an exploratory difference in within-slice model gains, not proof of a query bottleneck or an interaction effect. Retrieve evidence to distinguish insufficient relevant input, weak query construction, and loss of explicit relevance signals before choosing a mechanism.
